one_liner: Fuses OCaml lexer and parser via MetaOCaml staging, generating token-free code 2-6x faster than ocamlyacc.
what_it_does: flap is an OCaml parser-generator library that fuses lexing and parsing into one generated recognizer instead of a separate tokenize-then-parse pipeline. Grammars are written as combinator terms (eps, tok, >>>, <|>, star, fix) inside a Parse functor parameterized over a token-tag type, not as .mll/.mly grammar files. compile takes the lexer's regex/tag table and a typed parser term and returns a MetaOCaml quoted function ((string -> 'a) code), or an Error string if the grammar is ambiguous or left-recursive; the quotation still needs a MetaOCaml stager to become runnable OCaml code.
how_it_is_fast: The grammar is converted to Greibach Normal Form so the recognizer only ever needs one token of lookahead (a deterministic GNF, DGNF), letting the compiler generate a flat, branch-predictable recognizer instead of a table-driven automaton. Lexing and parsing are fused during code generation, so no intermediate token stream or token allocation is produced between the two phases. BER MetaOCaml multi-stage programming then specializes and unrolls this recognizer into monomorphic native code per grammar, removing the interpretive/dispatch overhead that generic combinator libraries and ocamlyacc/menhir's generated tables carry.
when_to_use: Parsing in OCaml where the grammar is a deterministic context-free grammar with one-token lookahead (structured formats like CSV, JSON, S-expressions, PGN, Netpbm-style binary/text formats)
Throughput-bound batch parsing of many or large documents (paper measures linear scaling up to ~2 MB inputs) where generated-code specialization amortizes
Already using, or willing to adopt, the BER MetaOCaml staged-compilation toolchain
Want to beat ocamlyacc- or menhir-generated parsers without hand-writing a bespoke recursive-descent parser
Research or prototyping context where an abandoned, single-author artifact (79 stars, MIT) is an acceptable dependency to read or vendor from
when_not_to_use: Need an actively maintained, supported parsing library — last commit 2023-07-01, no releases beyond the PLDI 2023 artifact
Grammar is ambiguous, needs backtracking/GLR-style resolution, or requires more than one token of lookahead — flap's <|> alternatives must be disjoint (not both nullable, non-overlapping first sets)
Need the parser usable from C/C++ or any non-OCaml host; there is no FFI story, it is OCaml-only
Cannot install a nonstandard compiler variant — flap requires the BER MetaOCaml switch (4.11.1+BER, optionally +flambda, or 4.14.1+BER), not stock OCaml
Generated code size matters: GNF conversion plus lexer/parser fusion can duplicate grammar productions

integration.dependencies: letrec, reex, reex_match, ppx_deriving (opam, runtime); ounit (test-only)
integration.min_toolchain: BER MetaOCaml N111 (opam-variants 4.11.1+BER, +flambda optional, or 4.14.1+BER); dune >= 2.9 with menhir 2.0 integration (used for the benchmark comparisons, not the library itself)
integration.platforms: CI only exercises ubuntu-latest (x86-64 Linux) with ocaml-variants.4.11.1+BER; macOS/Windows/ARM support not documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — different interface: grammars are OCaml combinator terms compiled through MetaOCaml staging, not ocamlyacc/menhir .mly/.mll grammar files

gotchas: compile returns Error string rather than raising when the grammar is ambiguous or left-recursive, so grammar bugs surface as a typing/compile-time result, not a parser exception
<|> alternatives must be manually kept disjoint (no shared first token, not both nullable); the library does not infer this for you
Requires the nonstandard BER MetaOCaml compiler switch; it will not build against a stock ocaml/opam toolchain
Runtime dependencies (reex, reex_match, letrec) are also single-author (yallop) packages, adding transitive maintenance risk beyond flap itself
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued siblings (re2c, lexy, winnow, chumsky, MPL, PAPAGENO, Pika Parser) target C or Rust and aren't usable from OCaml, so there's no direct substitution; pick flap specifically when you're already in OCaml, your grammar is a deterministic single-token-lookahead CFG, and you want to beat ocamlyacc/menhir rather than hand-roll a recursive-descent parser.
verified_claims_summary: PLDI 2023 paper benchmarks six grammars (JSON, CSV, S-expressions, PGN, Netpbm PPM, an arithmetic language) with Core_bench on one core of an Intel i9-12900K (1 GB RAM, Debian Linux), compiled with BER MetaOCaml N111 + flambda and -O3; flap's fused, staged code reached 1.9x-6.5x the throughput of ocamlyacc-generated parsers per grammar (e.g. ~5.8x on JSON, ~6.5x on PPM, ~1.9x on the arithmetic grammar) and also beat both menhir table- and code-generation backends.
status_note: Abandoned: no commits since 2023-07-01, existing only as the code artifact for a single PLDI 2023 paper. MIT-licensed and small enough to read or vendor, but the BER MetaOCaml toolchain requirement makes it high-friction to actually build on.
